samples.summary: Apply guard adds a new, much-later call to `editor.getLinkAtCursor()`, which is implemented on top of the *throwing* `Doc.getBlock` — a caret whose block has since disappeared turns Apply into an exception in a React click handler
samples.evidence: The guard's callee is `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3713-3715`: `getLinkAtCursor` does `const block = doc.getBlock(cursor.position.blockId); if (!block) return undefined;` — but `Doc.getBlock` (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:202-216`) *throws* `Block not found: …` when the id is gone, so the `if (!block)` guard is dead (an archived task doc, docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260728-docs-edit-link-in-place-todo.md:135, already records it as dead). Before this change the only caller was `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:465`, invoked synchronously at ⌘K time when the caret is certainly valid. The new call at `docs-link-popover.tsx:169` runs seconds later — the popover deliberately stays open while the caret moves, and a remote peer's block delete or a local undo in that window leaves `cursor.position.blockId` pointing at a removed block. `handleApply` then throws out of an onClick instead of showing the intended error. Fix belongs either in the new guard (wrap/soft-fail) or by making `getLinkAtCursor` use `doc.findBlock`, as the text-box variant already does (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1250).

samples.summary: The 'mouse left the table' drag branch still writes the range with a bare `selection.setRange`, bypassing the new `setSnappedRange` link expansion the rest of the pointer paths were converted to
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2363-2369` sets `{ anchor: { blockId: tableBlockId, offset: 0 }, focus: pos }` directly and returns, with no `expandRangeForLinks` and no `rawAnchor` write, while every other pointer path in the same handler now goes through `setSnappedRange` (2239, 2373, 1990, 2000, 2016, 2052, 2068). `pos` here is a body position that can land mid-link, so the invariant the change advertises — 'a pointer selection never partially covers a link', which `insertLink`'s `linkRunCoveringRange` branch keys off — is false on this path. A `mouseup` on that frame leaves the partially-covered selection standing; a further mousemove re-enters the snapped path, so the window is narrow.

samples.summary: `initializeTextBox`'s *selection* branch of `insertLink` was not given the `linkRunCoveringRange` treatment editor.ts got, even though the same shared `TextEditor` now snaps text-box drags to whole links
samples.evidence: The text box builds a `TextEditor` with its own `Selection` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:480, 668-672), so the new `setSnappedRange`/`expandRangeForLinks` behaviour applies there too and 'a drag over a link yields a selection exactly equal to the link' is now the normal shape in text boxes. But `text-box-editor.ts:1187-1193` still does only `doc.applyInlineStyle(range, { href: url })`, so a drag-selected self-labelled link keeps its stale old URL as display text — the very #1038 Part A bug fixed in `editor.ts:3612`. Reachability is currently low: slides leaves `onLinkRequest` unwired (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:738-741), so only the docs text-box API surface reaches it.
searchedFor: grep insertLink across packages/frontend and packages/slides

samples.summary: New comment (and the matching one in link-run.ts) describes `getBlockIndex` as unable to order two header/footer blocks — it can, because `getBlockIndex` is edit-context aware, so the documented 'left alone' case does not exist
samples.evidence: `Doc.getBlockIndex` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:271-273) indexes into `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:158-162), which returns `document.header.blocks` while `editContext === 'header'`. So a header drag spanning two header paragraphs *is* orderable and `expandRangeForLinks` *does* snap it, contrary to the comment at text-editor.ts:2235-2238 and the reasoning in packages/docs/src/view/link-run.ts:~170-180 ('a range spanning two blocks inside one table cell (or a header/footer region) is unorderable here'). Only the cell-block case is genuinely unorderable. A future reader trusting the comment will mis-reason about which ranges snap.

finding.summary: Apply guard adds a new, much-later call to `editor.getLinkAtCursor()`, which is implemented on top of the *throwing* `Doc.getBlock` — a caret whose block has since disappeared turns Apply into an exception in a React click handler
finding.evidence: The guard's callee is `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3713-3715`: `getLinkAtCursor` does `const block = doc.getBlock(cursor.position.blockId); if (!block) return undefined;` — but `Doc.getBlock` (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:202-216`) *throws* `Block not found: …` when the id is gone, so the `if (!block)` guard is dead (an archived task doc, docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260728-docs-edit-link-in-place-todo.md:135, already records it as dead). Before this change the only caller was `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:465`, invoked synchronously at ⌘K time when the caret is certainly valid. The new call at `docs-link-popover.tsx:169` runs seconds later — the popover deliberately stays open while the caret moves, and a remote peer's block delete or a local undo in that window leaves `cursor.position.blockId` pointing at a removed block. `handleApply` then throws out of an onClick instead of showing the intended error. verdict.reason: All cited code is present exactly as described. getLinkAtCursor (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3713-3715) resolves the caret block with the throwing Doc.getBlock (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:202-216, which ends in `throw new Error(`Block not found: ...`)`), making its `if (!block) return undefined` dead; the text-box twin at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1249-1251 uses the non-throwing doc.findBlock, and the archived task note at docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260728-docs-edit-link-in-place-todo.md:135 already flags the dead guard. The new Apply guard at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:169 calls getLinkAtCursor from a React click/Enter handler long after open — the component comment at lines 46-56 says the popover deliberately stays open while the caret moves — so a caret whose block disappeared turns Apply into an uncaught exception instead of the intended applyError. The repo itself treats cursor.position.blockId as stale-able at React time: editor.ts:3411, 3423, 3460 all use findBlock with a live fallback, and editor.ts:2557-2562 / 2762-2767 explicitly say "findBlock, not getBlock: the latter throws". I could not refute: mitigations exist (docs-view.tsx:419 validateCursorPosition on remote change, editor.ts:1126-1134; undo/redo re-homing at editor.ts:2340-2352 and 2376-2388; and insertLink already calls getBlock at editor.ts:3644 so the handler could throw pre-change), but validateCursorPosition no-ops on a zero-block context and find-bar mutations bypass editor entry points (editor.ts:1453-1458), so I cannot show the throwing path unreachable. Uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: Header/footer drag selection bypasses the new link snapping, so the "a pointer selection never partially covers a link" invariant the rest of the change relies on is reachable-false there
finding.evidence: `updateDragSelection`'s header/footer branch writes the range directly: `this.selection.setRange({ anchor: this.selection.range.anchor, focus: pos })` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2232), returning before the `setSnappedRange` call at 2360. The mousedown path for header/footer *does* fall through to the snapping code (the header/footer handling at 1914-1944 falls through to the shared block at 2049+), so press-snaps then drag-unsnaps, and it also clears `rawAnchor` on every mousemove (`setRange` now nulls it, selection.ts:712). A partially covered link selection in a header/footer then reaches `editor.insertLink`, whose new `linkRunCoveringRange` branch (editor.ts:3612) declines it and falls through to the wide-span path — the exact stale-display-text state #1038 claims to have made unreachable.

verdict.reason: The bypassing site the finding names does not exist. In `updateDragSelection`, the header/footer branch (text-editor.ts:2223-2250) does NOT write the range directly — it calls `this.setSnappedRange({ anchor: this.selection.range.anchor, focus: pos })` at text-editor.ts:2239-2242. The line the finding cites as the raw `selection.setRange(...)` write (2232) is actually the comment documenting the opposite ("Snapped like the body drag below... so 'a pointer selection never partially covers a link' (#1038) has to hold in this context as well"). There is no `selection.setRange` call anywhere in that branch. Consequently the secondary claims also fail: `setSnappedRange` (text-editor.ts:2394-2400) re-stores `this.selection.rawAnchor` immediately after `setRange`, so `rawAnchor` is not cleared on each header/footer mousemove and there is no press-snap/drag-unsnap asymmetry. Because the header/footer drag range is already snapped, `linkRunCoveringRange` at editor.ts:3612 is not reached with a partially-covering range from this path, so the stale-display-text state is not reachable via the route described. The only direct `selection.setRange(...)` left inside `updateDragSelection` is at text-editor.ts:2363-2366, which is the body-context "mouse left the table" whole-block table highlight — a different branch, not the header/footer path this finding is about. Corroborating: packages/docs/test/view/link-snap-header-drag.test.ts:167-193 drives real mousedown/mousemove in header edit context and asserts snapping of both anchor and focus plus correct un-snapping.
